Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — latency questions you raised

Hi Liz / Acme SRE team —

Thanks for the clear asks. I ran the microbenchmark suite we discussed against the candidate config and attached the PDF with full telemetry. High-level summary:

Test configuration:
- Model: open-redwood-1.7B (production-quantized q4_0)
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 80GB (single-gpu node)
- Sequence length: 1,024 tokens (prompt + generation), typical payload used in your demo
- Batching: dynamic continuous batching (observed batch sizes 1–8)
- KV cache: measured warm vs cold scenarios

Results (single-node, median of 10 runs):
- P50 latency: ~42 ms / token (warm cache)
- P95 latency: ~125 ms / token (observed spikes when background compile + cache cold)
- P99 latency: ~240 ms / token (rare GC/compile edge cases)
- Max throughput (sustained): ~1100 tokens/s for batch size 8

Notes and recommendations:
- You’ll see the biggest wins by enabling our prefix cache for repetitive prompts — reduces P95 by ~30% in our tests.
- Quantized runtime (q4) yields ~1.8x token/s vs float16 for your sequence lengths at similar tail-latency characteristics.
- For tighter P95 SLAs, we recommend a small dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs) with pinned warm worker slots to avoid cold-start spikes.

I attached the PDF with raw numbers, graphs, and the exact command lines (cc-curves, p95 timeline). If you want, we can reproduce the same harness on a small dedicated pool for you to validate the numbers under your network conditions.

Ben
Bench Lead, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood-latency-report-20260218.pdf (pdf, 320KB)]
